title: Case report: A novel technique of robotic low-tension hiatal hernia repair using mediastinoplication
author: Domene, Madalosso, et al.

steps.title: Position patient and induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the patient supine on the operating table, induce general anesthesia, and prepare for robotic access.

steps.title: Create pneumoperitoneum and insert trocars
steps.instruction: Insufflate the abdomen to establish pneumoperitoneum, then insert the robotic trocars according to the planned configuration.

steps.title: Dissect and mobilize hernia sac
steps.instruction: Perform a complete dissection of the hiatal hernia sac, carefully preserving surrounding structures such as the vagus nerves, and fully mobilize the sac from the mediastinum to expose the crura and esophagus.

substeps.instruction: Identify the large hiatal defect and the herniated stomach.
Release the hernia sac from mediastinal attachments while protecting the vagus nerves.
Mobilize the sac completely to obtain clear exposure of the crura and esophagus.

steps.title: Mobilize esophagus within mediastinum
steps.instruction: Dissect the esophagus free from all mediastinal attachments to obtain sufficient intra‑abdominal length for a tension‑free repair.

steps.title: Perform mediastinoplication with barbed sutures
steps.instruction: Using barbed sutures, plicate the mediastinal fibers, mediastinal pleura, and pericardium on both the right and left sides of the esophagus, placing separate sutures on each side to obliterate the residual mediastinal space and reduce its volume.

steps.title: Repair crura with non‑absorbable sutures
steps.instruction: Approximate the right and left crura without tension using interrupted non‑absorbable sutures; then pass a bougie through the hiatus and repeat suturing until the esophagus passes freely with adequate lumen.

substeps.instruction: Bring the right and left crura together and place interrupted non‑absorbable sutures.
Insert a bougie through the hiatus to test patency.
Adjust and add sutures as needed until the bougie passes without constriction and the hiatus is tension‑free.

steps.title: Construct Nissen fundoplication
steps.instruction: Wrap the mobilized stomach 360° around the abdominal esophagus to create a tension‑free valve, completing the fundoplication.

steps.title: Post‑operative care and discharge
steps.instruction: Extubate the patient in the operating room, start a liquid diet, advance to soft solids over one week, and discharge on postoperative day 2; schedule follow‑up imaging and endoscopy to confirm adequate hiatus calibration.
